- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.33) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes — model often overshoots then corrects downward, but fails to fully adjust early.
- Overforecast in the short-term (1-3 days) after recent price spikes — model exhibits lagged mean reversion bias.
- Underforecast in the long-term (10+ days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00), model tends to overestimate — likely due to lack of downward bias correction.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in 30-day horizon — especially when sentiment is flat or mildly bullish.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — if sentiment rises, model often forecasts higher than true outcome until 3-5 days later.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts — true outcomes often show mean reversion toward 70–75 range after 10+ days of high prices.
- If sentiment is 1.00 (strong bullish), model should not forecast >10% above recent high — overestimation is common.
- When sentiment is 0.00, model should not forecast >5% above recent low — underestimation is common.
